findings.description: The instance's user_data embeds a plaintext AWS access key ID and secret access key (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA / wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMAAAKEY). User data is readable via instance metadata and the EC2 API, so anyone with access to the instance or console can harvest long-lived credentials.
The security group opens SSH (tcp/22) to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and exploitation attempts from the entire internet.
HTTP (tcp/80) is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, publishing the Apache service directly to the internet.
The EBS volume has no encrypted = true setting, so data on the attached disk is stored unencrypted at rest and can be read from snapshots.

findings.issue_category: Missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, no public access block, and force_destroy = true, leaving log data unencrypted and potentially world-accessible or destructible.
The snapshot is created without encryption, so a copy of the unencrypted volume data can be shared or restored elsewhere.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, removing a layer of isolation for workloads that should not be internet-facing.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true makes every instance in this subnet internet-addressable by default.
